title: Real-time Collaborative Inventory Dashboard
business: Warehouse logistics managers overseeing high-velocity inventory turnover.
problem: Traditional polling-based web interfaces cause stale data displays, leading to shipment errors when multiple operators update stock levels simultaneously.
solution: Phoenix Channels provide a persistent, bidirectional communication layer between the server and client, allowing the server to push inventory updates to all connected browser sessions instantly.
steps: Define a Phoenix Channel module to handle incoming socket connections and topic subscriptions.
Configure the UserSocket to route incoming messages to the appropriate channel based on the inventory category.
Implement the handle_in callback to process stock adjustment requests from the client.
Use the Phoenix.PubSub broadcast mechanism to push state changes to all clients subscribed to a specific inventory topic.
Update the client-side LiveView or JavaScript interface to reflect the pushed data without requiring a full page refresh.
outcome: Operators experience a synchronized view of inventory levels, ensuring that stock adjustments are visible across all terminals in real-time.
limitation: Maintaining thousands of persistent socket connections consumes significant server memory; monitor the process count and memory usage via the Observer tool to ensure the system remains stable under high load.

diagram.title: Inventory Update Flow
diagram.description: This diagram illustrates how an inventory change propagates through the Phoenix system.

code.content:
def handle_in("update_stock", payload, socket) do
  # Broadcast the new stock level to all subscribers of this topic
  Phoenix.PubSub.broadcast(MyApp.PubSub, "inventory", {:stock_updated, payload})
  {:noreply, socket}
end
code.explanation: This code demonstrates how a channel receives an update and broadcasts it to all connected clients, mapping directly to the solution of pushing real-time inventory changes.
